rows.grounds: demonstrative referring to previously mentioned items

items.question: How should all these items be arranged for Śiva worship?
premises: All these items are intended for Śiva worship.
Arrangement must follow appropriateness.
The practitioner should arrange them accordingly.
items.inference: Therefore all these items should be arranged suitably for the purpose of Śiva worship.
items.plain_english: One should arrange all this appropriately for the purpose of Śiva worship.

rows.grounds: compound: loha+member, ja+head; object to be offered

items.question: Where should metal-born and stone-born items be offered in worship?
premises: A metal-born item is to be offered at the door.
A stone-born item is to be offered in the enclosure.
The two materials have distinct placement locations.
items.inference: Therefore metal-born items should be offered at the door and stone-born items in the enclosure.
items.plain_english: One should offer the metal-made item at the door, but the stone-made item in the surrounding enclosure.

items.question: What sonic elements must precede the mantra at the beginning?
premises: The mantra is joined with bindu and nāda.
It is placed at the beginning.
It is preceded by the praṇava.
items.inference: Therefore the mantra should begin with praṇava and be joined with bindu and nāda.
items.plain_english: At the beginning, it should be preceded by the praṇava and joined with bindu and nāda.

rows.grounds: instrumental use of the astra mantra

items.question: What ritual sequence must precede worship of the door guardians?
premises: The door must be sprinkled with the astra mantra.
The door guardians are the objects of worship.
Worship must proceed in order.
items.inference: Therefore after sprinkling the door with the astra mantra, one should worship the door guardians in order.
items.plain_english: Having sprinkled the door with the astra mantra, one should worship the door guardians in due order.

items.question: On which sides should Mahākāla and Yamunā be worshipped?
premises: Mahākāla is associated with the right side.
Yamunā is associated with the left side.
Both should be worshipped.
items.inference: Therefore one should worship Mahākāla on the right and Yamunā on the left.
items.plain_english: One should worship Mahākāla on the right side and Yamunā on the left side.

items.inference: Therefore these deities should be worshipped in order with mantras ending in obeisance and with the heart mantra and others.
items.plain_english: These should be worshipped in proper order with mantras ending in obeisance and with the heart mantra and the others.

items.question: What action with the sword addresses the threefold obstacles?

A sword is to be placed.

items.inference: Therefore the excellent hidden cloth should be placed at the end of twilight.

items.question: What previously arranged worship located in the liṅga must be addressed?
premises: Worship was previously arranged in the middle of the liṅga.
That worship was established at an earlier time.
It is the object of the subsequent ritual action.
items.inference: Therefore the worship previously arranged in the middle of the liṅga must be ritually dismissed.
items.plain_english: The worship previously arranged in the middle of the liṅga at an earlier time must be addressed.

The worship must be released from the liṅga.

items.plain_english: Having uttered the five brahmans, one should release the worship from the liṅga.

items.question: To whom and by what means should the pedestal be ritually placed?

The placement is directed to Caṇḍeśa.
The action is performed through application of the astra mantra.
items.inference: Therefore the pedestal should be placed for Caṇḍeśa through application of the astra mantra.
items.plain_english: Having placed the pedestal for Caṇḍeśa through the application of the astra mantra.

premises: The Śiva liṅga must be purified.

items.plain_english: Having purified the Śiva liṅga together with its platform with water empowered by the astra mantra.

items.question: What seat should be arranged for the bathing rite invocation?
premises: An invocation seat is required in the bathing rite.
The seat takes the form of a lotus.
The seat is associated with Ananta.
items.inference: Therefore in the bathing rite one should arrange a lotus invocation seat upon Ananta.
uncertainties: Whether anantam qualifies the lotus or names a distinct support is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: In the bathing rite, the invocation seat should be a lotus upon Ananta.

items.question: Where should garments and other ritual acts be arranged?

items.inference: Therefore garments and other ritual acts should be arranged on the lion throne.
items.plain_english: One should arrange garments and the other ritual acts on the lion throne.

items.question: Is any form of worship other than Śaiva worship prescribed?
premises: Śaiva worship is to be performed.
Scriptural prescription governs the rite.

items.plain_english: Śaiva worship must be performed; no other form is prescribed.

items.plain_english: The seat is declared to be twofold, based on the distinction between body and soul.

items.plain_english: One should contemplate the divine body that extends up to mahāmāyā.

items.question: What iconographic form should be contemplated in the heart?

It is joined with folded hands.
items.inference: Therefore one should contemplate in the heart a one-faced, four-armed form with folded hands.
items.plain_english: In the heart, one should contemplate a one-faced, four-armed form with hands joined in reverence.

premises: The manifestation has a lion form.
